checked_scope: An explicit, exponent-sharp modulus for robust digital-claim valuation under Wasserstein perturbations of entire admissible pricing-law sets. This addresses discontinuous payoffs left outside the prior finite-state interior-calibration theorem. It assumes, rather than derives, stability of the calibrated sets.
checks: Indicator disagreement is contained in {|X|<=r} union {|X-Y|>r}; coupling and Markov give Cr^beta+Wp^p/r^p. Differentiating in r gives the displayed K_(p,beta) and C exponent, including zero-distance and indicator cap cases.
Approximate nearest laws at distance delta+epsilon suffice for both directed sup/inf comparisons; continuity of omega allows epsilon down to zero without compactness or endpoint attainment.

The three-state laws have positive masses, common margin constant C=1 for every radius, and digital gap r^beta/2. At least r^beta/2 mass leaves -r over distance >=2r, proving the exact transport cost 2^(p-1)r^(p+beta) and exponent sharpness.

Endpoint errors imply width error <=2omega; expanding the estimated interval by omega per side gives true-set coverage and excess width <=4omega. This extends precisely the prior manuscript discontinuous-payoff limitation and assumes law-set stability.
